nodes.label: MH_01 Threshold Gate
nodes.rationale: Sweep only outlier_avg_reproj_px and select the tightest candidate that preserves the MH_01 hard gate before diagnosing MH_05.

nodes.label: Bounded Cull-LM Loop
nodes.rationale: Repeat permanent mean-cull and graph rebuild plus LM for at most max_outlier_reopts rounds while leaving observation-level flipping and Huber changes out of scope.

nodes.label: Mass-Cull Drop Gate
nodes.rationale: When mean-cull removes at least four landmarks, skip tracker dropTracks for that frame to avoid a post-cull track wipe while retaining block_culled_rebirth.

nodes.label: Pending Drop Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Accumulate skipped culled landmark IDs and flush them before the next tracker process call, with explicit deferred drop counters and no new configuration key.

nodes.label: Estimator-Only Divergence Replay
nodes.rationale: Capture the glue-boundary measurements and reproduce the first bad state in a deterministic sub-15-second estimator replay before ranking causal hypotheses.

nodes.label: Stereo RMS Proposal Gate
nodes.rationale: Treat left-camera PnP as a proposal and accept it only when full stereo RMS on the same inlier set is within one stereo noise band of the constant-velocity guess.

nodes.label: Track-Only Non-Keyframes
nodes.rationale: Select keyframes in the session from parallax, survival, and time while non-keyframes estimate pose through PnP without entering the BA window.

nodes.label: Rotation-Compensated Keyframe Selection
nodes.rationale: Repair the initial keyframe slice by pose-only non-keyframe refinement, low-shared rejection, rotation-compensated parallax, and snapshot updates only after accepted keyframes.

nodes.label: Basalt-Style Window Eviction
nodes.rationale: Let all accepted frames participate in BA while only keyframes seed landmarks, then enforce a seven-keyframe plus three-temporal-frame window.

nodes.label: M4 Phase Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Sequence remaining VO debt, keyframe design, then M4 as synchronizer, preintegration, initialization, and integration slices because the keyframe schedule defines IMU preintegration boundaries.

nodes.label: Motion-Adaptive Keyframe Threshold
nodes.rationale: Use a DKB-SLAM motion history to vary parallax threshold from 30 to 10 pixels and force a keyframe after more than 45 degrees of accumulated rotation.

nodes.label: Robust LK Tracking Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Harden V-series tracking with median-flow LK initialization, CLAHE, fundamental-matrix RANSAC, a lower GFTT quality threshold, and a deeper pyramid.

nodes.label: Zero-Disparity Hanging Tracks
nodes.rationale: Preserve stable tracks with no right match as zero-disparity observations, exclude them from stereo BA factors, and use them as multiframe triangulation candidates; the final composed gate retained this hanging-track carrier with distance and refresh controls.

nodes.label: Frontend Attribution A-B Matrix
nodes.rationale: First test the constant-velocity-chain contamination hypothesis from existing diagnostics, then isolate CLAHE, median flow, F-RANSAC, quality level, and pyramid depth with temporary one-variable experiments.

nodes.label: Boundary-Interpolated IMU Segments
nodes.rationale: Segment raw IMU samples at paired left-image timestamps, interpolate both boundaries, preserve sum-delta-time equality, and mark large gaps without yet consuming IMU in the estimator.

nodes.label: Combined IMU Factor Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Extend the window to X/V/B, rebuild preintegration from raw intervals, add CombinedImuFactor constraints, use IMU prediction for initialization, retain rejected-frame intervals in pending state, and retire visual re-anchor when IMU is enabled.

nodes.label: M4.3 Triple-Gate Result
nodes.rationale: Stationary initialization, dropout continuity, and bias diagnostics were implemented, but MH_01 and MH_05 quantitative gates failed while segment continuity and gyro-bias scale passed.

nodes.label: Behavior-Preserving Transaction Seam
nodes.rationale: Extract keyframe evidence, rule priority, and accepted-epoch commit into a move-only decide-resolve gate while requiring byte-identical MH_01 production artifacts.

nodes.label: Guard Non-Intervention Result
nodes.rationale: Collect IMU and pose-lag evidence under the fixed production schedule without changing decisions; the resulting evidence supported no production guard promotion.

nodes.label: Rule 4 Negative Result and Rollback
nodes.rationale: IMU derotation at 30, 15, and 10 pixels did not recover the MH_01 control ATE; production changes were rolled back byte-for-byte and successor work shifted to a behavior-preserving gate seam.

nodes.label: Duplicate Bias Factor Removal
nodes.rationale: Align the graph with the GTSAM CombinedImuFactor contract by deleting the additional bias BetweenFactor; the change slightly improved the VIO control but did not beat VO on common support.

nodes.label: Batch Twin Ownership Seam
nodes.rationale: Run an isolated candidate-owned tracker, gate, estimator, diagnostics, and trajectory beside production as an equivalent batch twin; require production byte identity before any fixed-lag replacement work.

nodes.label: Frontend-first Error Attribution
nodes.rationale: Fixed-window batch BA with robust loss is within the mainstream design envelope; the observed order-of-magnitude regression is more plausibly driven by frontend tracking collapse and missing recovery than by the backend objective.

nodes.label: Stereo Depth Starvation
nodes.rationale: Corridor sequences can retain healthy left-image temporal tracking while right-image SAD matching collapses, starving the estimator of metric stereo depth; temporal parallax should supplement disparity rather than treating all failures as cross-eye brightness problems.

nodes.label: Keyframe Failure Self-sustain Chain
nodes.rationale: Fast rotation churns track identities; rollback after the first keyframe BA failure prevents new IDs from entering the graph, overlap decays, accepted pose freezes, and stale constant-velocity reanchoring makes the failure persistent.

nodes.label: Zero-shared Landmark Absorbing State
nodes.rationale: Rejecting a frame when shared landmarks reach zero, while transaction rollback preserves the old map and the frontend continues issuing new IDs, creates a state from which normal overlap cannot recover.

nodes.label: Reanchor and Seed State Machine
nodes.rationale: Recovery removes the zero-shared absorbing gate, rebuilds a new observation window at a predicted pose, applies a minimum seed observation gate, and makes segment transitions diagnosable.

nodes.label: Zero-overlap Recovery Reference Patterns
nodes.rationale: Basalt, VINS, SVO, Kimera and ORB systems continue, force a keyframe, use inertial prediction, or split maps; none directly matches a single-trajectory last-accepted/CV reanchor without marginal priors or IMU.

nodes.label: Age-five Zombie Drop Policy
nodes.rationale: Dropping culled tracks only after five skipped frames preserves short-term recovery while preventing stale tracks from occupying the tracker indefinitely; it improved MH_05 and passed the MH_01 hard gate.

nodes.label: M4 Vertical-slice Contract
nodes.rationale: The design stages exact IMU packetization, estimator X/V/B integration, stationary initialization and keyframe-rule evaluation, while requiring IMU-off byte equivalence and explicit failure reporting.

nodes.label: Closed-loop Candidate Ownership
nodes.rationale: An accuracy counterfactual must branch at immutable rectified stereo plus IMU input and independently own tracker, identifiers, keyframe policy, estimator, landmark lifecycle, reset and trajectory; backend-only shadowing is diagnostic rather than a whole-system candidate.

nodes.label: Atomic Candidate Pipeline
nodes.rationale: A single process/finish seam in the apps composition root keeps tracking, gating, estimation, cull/drop feedback, reset, diagnostics and trajectory ownership inside one deep module without exposing a generic optimizer abstraction.

nodes.label: Batch Twin Ownership Equivalence
nodes.rationale: After candidate cull/drop/zombie feedback was made isomorphic to production, the independently owned batch twin matched production artifacts and per-frame behavior byte-for-byte on MH_01 without feeding state back.

nodes.label: Fixed-lag Candidate Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: P2b replaces the temporary batch twin with one concrete fixed-lag implementation that owns accepted epochs, per-state bias, factor slots, landmark generations, natural retirement, rollback and explicit resets, without a backend switch or fallback.

nodes.label: Fixed-lag Structure Gate Result
nodes.rationale: The candidate completed MH_01 with bounded state and no terminal failures, proving lifecycle structure, but exact-common ATE and RPE were substantially worse than paired VO, so the precision gate failed.

nodes.label: Duplicate Bias Constraint Removal
nodes.rationale: CombinedImuFactor already contains bias evolution, so the additional bias BetweenFactor double-counted the constraint; removing it corrected the model contract but did not make VIO beat VO.

nodes.label: IMU Factor Overconfidence
nodes.rationale: Millimeter-scale position disagreement produced orders-of-magnitude larger initial IMU cost than visual cost and was driven to micron residuals, indicating that raw PIM covariance did not express cross-sensor/model discrepancy.

nodes.label: Consistency Covariance Negative Result
nodes.rationale: Adding measured rotation/position/velocity consistency variance removed factor overconfidence, but both full-run and full-suffix ATE/RPE remained worse than VO; the arm was rejected and raw production covariance restored.

nodes.label: Fixed Accelerometer Bias Negative Result
nodes.rationale: Freezing accelerometer bias made translation accuracy much worse, showing that observed bias drift was a symptom rather than the primary cause and that some bias adjustment was needed by the current model.

nodes.label: Staged Full-inertial Activation
nodes.rationale: The estimator should progress from vision-only to gyro-visual and only then to full visual-inertial after a held-out alignment gate, using standard full ImuFactor without duplicating AHRS rotation constraints.

nodes.label: Boundary Robustification Negative Result
nodes.rationale: Accepted/rejected transition edges showed ordinary sub-sigma gyro residuals and no association with bad ATE buckets, so boundary-specific Huber or information scaling was rejected and the Gaussian AHRS factor retained.

nodes.label: Gyro Covariance and Bias Observability
nodes.rationale: Alignment disagreement is not sensor covariance, the tested covariance scale sweep had no dual-metric sweet spot, and a 0.5-second window cannot reliably observe per-frame gyro bias despite random-walk bias being the mature long-term model.

nodes.label: Installed GTSAM Fixed-lag Contracts
nodes.rationale: Five tests lock strict cutoff, refreshed shared-key fixation, reusable factor slots, timestamp orphan failure and snapshot rollback across the actual installed GTSAM library before any runtime shadow is attempted.

nodes.label: Fixed-lag Lifecycle Constraints
nodes.rationale: A direct solver swap is unsafe because shared bias becomes fixed, explicit landmark removal can orphan timestamps, post-opt cull cannot retract information already absorbed into a marginal prior, and failed updates require whole-smoother plus ledger rollback.
